newsitem.title: BRAZIL: Brazil to begin AIDS education with 4-year-olds.
newsitem.headline: Brazil to begin AIDS education with 4-year-olds.

text.p: Brazilian children as young as 4 years old will be the target of the government's new AIDS awareness campaigns in 1997, officials said on Friday.

The government will also distribute 250 million free condoms to groups considered to be at risk from AIDS including prisoners, prostitutes, wildcat miners and Indians in some of Brazil's remote regions and women living in big city slums.
"Brazilians have heard of the word AIDS but they're not aware of how it is transmitted," said Pedro Paulo Santanna, a spokesman for the Health Ministry's AIDS programme.

Brazil has one of the world's highest rates of HIV infection with 90,000 cases officially registered. The government estimates that out of a population of 160 million, as many as 450,000 people have the virus.

In an attempt to raise AIDS awareness, schoolchildren between ages 4 and 6 will be taught the biological differences between boys and girls, while those from 7 to 9 will learn about the disease and be shown how to use condoms, Santanna said.
Some 1.4 million pamphlets aimed at children from 4 to 19 will be distributed in schools to help get the AIDS message across, he said.
